overview: EBOS Group is the largest and most diversified Australasian marketer, wholesaler, and distributor of healthcare, medical, and pharmaceutical products, with a leading position in animal care distribution. With over 5,700 employees across Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia, EBOS operates through two main segments: Healthcare (pharmaceutical wholesale, hospital distribution, medical technology including spine and oncology, retail pharmacy networks TerryWhite Chemmart and MediAdvice, contract logistics) and Animal Care (branded pet foods including Black Hawk and VitaPet, and veterinary supplies distribution via Lyppard and SVS). The company is dual-listed on the NZX and ASX and reports in Australian dollars.
thesis_alert: FY2026 full-year results (released 19 August 2026) confirmed successful completion of the four-year, A$360M distribution centre renewal program on time and within budget, with FY2026 underlying EBITDA of A$614M (+5.0%) landing within the (downgraded) A$610-620M guidance range, and management RAISING FY2027 underlying EBITDA guidance to A$635-655M (~5% growth) with FY2027 capex guided down to ~A$100M (from ~A$145M). This is a confirmation, not a break, of the prior 'FY2027 free-cash-flow inflection' thesis -- the DC investment cycle is now behind the company. However, two new items warrant attention: (1) a SECOND, smaller Chemist Warehouse contract loss -- this time the New Zealand wholesale contract, scheduled to roll off end of calendar 2026, sized by management at ~1% of group EBITDA (mid-to-high single-digit A$ millions) -- immaterial individually but a recurring pattern with this customer; and (2) the stock has re-rated sharply lower, trading roughly 30-45% below its 52-week high (~NZ$41.98) at a recent price near NZ$29-30, with consensus analyst price targets trimmed from the ~NZ$33-38 range six months ago to an average around NZ$29.60-31.40. The de-rating appears to be a multiple/sentiment reset (structural GOR margin compression from GLP-1/high-value-medicine mix, and skepticism about the FY2027 cash inflection actually showing up) rather than a fresh operational or corporate-action shock. No takeover approach, delisting, or equity raise occurred in the period. DCF assumptions (growth, WACC, terminal growth) likely still hold directionally given guidance was delivered and raised, but the base-year FCF and near-term multiple should be refreshed against actual FY2026 numbers (underlying FCF A$241M, reported FCF A$204M, leverage 2.1x) rather than the prior H1 FY2026 negative-FCF snapshot, and the model should reflect the lower current market price as a valuation check.

business_model.summary: EBOS operates a diversified distribution and retail model with the large majority of revenue from Healthcare and a smaller but fast-growing Animal Care segment (Animal Care revenue +34.6% in FY2026, aided by SVS and bolt-on M&A). Revenue is generated through wholesale distribution margins regulated by PBS/PHARMAC frameworks, retail pharmacy franchise operations, medical technology partnerships, branded product sales in animal care, and contract logistics services.

revenue_streams.name: Community Pharmacy Wholesale
revenue_streams.description: Distribution to independent pharmacies in Australia and New Zealand. FY2026 community pharmacy revenue A$7.1B (whole group), up 10.2%. TerryWhite Chemmart banner sales A$2.9B (+9.2%), dispensing sales +8.5%. Growth driven by GLP-1 and high-value medicines, but FY2026 group gross operating revenue (GOR) margin compressed 40bps to 12.9% reflecting mix shift toward lower-margin, higher-absolute-dollar medicines.

revenue_streams.name: Institutional Healthcare
revenue_streams.description: Distribution to hospitals and aged care, plus Medical Technology. FY2026 saw record hospital sales and continued MedTech therapy/geographic expansion (spine, urology, oncology, Southeast Asia, aesthetics via K-Talyst).

revenue_streams.name: Contract Logistics
revenue_streams.description: 3PL/4PL services including clinical trial logistics, cold chain. Expanding through FY2026 with new Perth facility and continued principal wins; high-value/temperature-controlled medicines driving growth.

revenue_streams.name: Animal Care - Branded Products
revenue_streams.description: Branded pet foods (Black Hawk, VitaPet) and treats. New entry into premium fresh/chilled pet food via the Paringa Pet Foods acquisition (completed July 2026, cleared by ACCC), expanding the branded portfolio's addressable market.

revenue_streams.name: Animal Care - Wholesale
revenue_streams.description: Veterinary wholesale distribution via Lyppard and SVS. FY2026 Animal Care segment revenue A$907M (+34.6%), EBITDA A$138M (+11.6%), reflecting a full year of SVS plus bolt-on additions.

business_model.customer_type: B2B primarily (pharmacies, hospitals, veterinary clinics, retailers) with B2C through TerryWhite Chemmart and MediAdvice pharmacy networks
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia ~75%, New Zealand and others ~25%. Southeast Asia exposure growing via MedTech (K-Talyst aesthetics distribution) but still small.
business_model.margin_profile: FY2026 underlying EBITDA margin 4.6% (Healthcare division EBITDA A$516M on A$12.6B revenue, +3.2% EBITDA growth on +8.5% revenue growth -- continued negative operating leverage as GOR margin compresses). Group GOR margin fell 40bps to 12.9% in FY2026 on GLP-1/high-value-medicine mix. Animal Care EBITDA margin materially higher than Healthcare and improving. Now that the DC renewal program is complete, management guides to margin recovery via utilisation/productivity gains (Kemps Creek already ~20% more productive than the facility it replaced, targeting 30% uplift by end of FY2027).

main_competitors: Sigma Healthcare (merged with Chemist Warehouse in 2024-2025, ~35-40% pharmacy wholesale market share)
API (owned by Wesfarmers since 2022, operates Priceline Pharmacy network)
National Veterinary Care (NVS) in animal health
Greencross (owned by TPG Capital) in pet retail and veterinary services
DHL Supply Chain / Toll Group in healthcare contract logistics
competitive_position.market_position: Largest healthcare distributor in Australia and New Zealand by network breadth. Leading position in hospital distribution and medical technology (spine implantables, and now aesthetics via K-Talyst in Southeast Asia/Hong Kong). TerryWhite Chemmart and MediAdvice combined form a ~780-store pharmacy retail network (up 86 stores in FY2026). In animal care, EBOS holds the #1 position in premium dry dog food in ANZ pet specialty through Black Hawk, now expanding into fresh/chilled pet food via Paringa.
competitive_position.market_share: Approximately 30-35% of pharmaceutical wholesale market in ANZ following the 2024 Australian Chemist Warehouse contract loss. Sigma-Chemist Warehouse entity holds 35-40% of the Australian wholesale market. EBOS's smaller New Zealand wholesale contract with Chemist Warehouse is also scheduled to roll off at the end of calendar 2026 (management-sized impact ~1% of group EBITDA), continuing a pattern of Chemist Warehouse consolidating supply in-house as it scales. EBOS remains a leading surgical implantables partner in APAC for Medical Technology.

moat_factors.description: The A$360 million, four-year distribution centre renewal program is now COMPLETE as confirmed at FY2026 results (19 August 2026), the largest capital cycle in company history. Kemps Creek (largest, most complex site) is running approximately 20% more productively than the Greystanes facility it replaced, with management targeting a 30% productivity uplift by the end of FY2027. This is now a realized, not promised, infrastructure and cost advantage, and a meaningful barrier to entry versus smaller competitors.

Pharmaceutical wholesale requires extensive licensing, GDP compliance, controlled substance permits, and temperature-controlled logistics capabilities. EBOS's participation in the Australian PBS Community Service Obligation (CSO) framework and NZ PHARMAC distribution arrangements provides contractual certainty. The expanded CSO regime effective July 2026 (covering Section 100 Medicines, higher high-cost medicine cap) is a structural positive now in effect.

As the largest healthcare distributor in ANZ, EBOS benefits from economies of scale in logistics, procurement, and systems, now amplified by the completed DC automation program. The breadth of service across community pharmacy, hospital, medical technology, contract logistics, and animal care creates cross-selling and bundling opportunities unavailable to smaller competitors.

Long-term relationships with hospitals, pharmacies, and veterinary clinics; integrated ordering/inventory systems create switching costs. However, the pending loss of the smaller NZ Chemist Warehouse wholesale contract (rolling off end of calendar 2026) is a reminder that even long-standing relationships are vulnerable once a customer reaches the scale to vertically integrate its own supply chain.

moat_factors.factor: Vertical integration across healthcare value chain
moat_factors.description: Ownership of wholesale distribution (Symbion), medical technology distribution, retail pharmacy networks (TWC, MediAdvice), contract logistics, and animal care manufacturing/distribution creates synergies unavailable to single-segment players.

Black Hawk is the leading premium pet food in ANZ by volume in pet specialty; VitaPet is a leading pet treat brand in NZ supermarkets. The Paringa Pet Foods acquisition (completed July 2026, ACCC-cleared) extends the branded portfolio into the growing premium fresh/chilled pet food category.

moat_factors.factor: Medical technology biologics and aesthetics platform
moat_factors.description: Origin Biologics (US allograft) consolidated December 2025; K-Talyst (medical device and aesthetics distribution across Southeast Asia/Hong Kong) acquired in FY2026, accelerating entry into the high-growth aesthetics sector. Biologics, aesthetics, and MedTech remain structurally higher-margin than core pharmaceutical wholesale.

weaknesses: Track record of losing large distribution contracts to Chemist Warehouse as that customer vertically integrates: the 2024 Australian loss (~A$1.9B revenue, ~10% of group) is now compounded by a second, smaller New Zealand wholesale contract set to roll off end of calendar 2026 (~1% of group EBITDA) -- a recurring, if now much smaller, pattern

Regulated wholesale GOR margins under the 1PWA framework, plus GLP-1/high-value-medicine mix shift, continue to compress group GOR margin (down 40bps to 12.9% in FY2026) even as revenue grows strongly -- Healthcare EBITDA grew only 3.2% against 8.5% revenue growth in FY2026, showing persistent negative operating leverage

Significant share price de-rating over the past six to twelve months (roughly 30-45% below the 52-week high of ~NZ$41.98, trading near NZ$29-30 as of September 2026) despite the DC program completing successfully and FY2027 guidance being raised, suggesting the market has become more skeptical about margin recovery timing or GLP-1 mix economics

Geographic concentration - primarily exposed to Australia and New Zealand economies with limited international diversification beyond early-stage Southeast Asia and a small US biologics/allograft foothold
Animal Care segment margin mix diluted by lower-margin SVS/wholesale contribution, though branded and fresh/chilled additions (Paringa) are intended to offset this over time

growth_drivers: DC renewal program complete, driving realized (not just promised) operational leverage: the four-year, A$360M program finished within FY2026, on time and within budget. Kemps Creek already running ~20% more productively than the facility it replaced, targeting 30% uplift by end of FY2027. FY2027 capex guided down to ~A$100M from ~A$145M, a ~30% reduction that management says will flow directly into free cash flow.

GLP-1 and high-value medicine structural growth continuing at double-digit rates in FY2026. Management noted EBOS 'indexes slightly low' in GLP-1 share specifically but over-indexes in medicines exceeding A$1,000 per dose, meaning the mix shift toward high-value medicines is a larger driver of gross profit dollars than GLP-1 alone, even though it compresses percentage GOR margin.

Medical Technology and aesthetics expansion: K-Talyst acquisition (Southeast Asia/Hong Kong medical device and aesthetics distribution) opens a new, high-growth therapy category. AlphaXRT (radiation oncology) and Precision Surgical (spine) from H1 FY2026 continue to broaden therapy areas. Origin Biologics gives US allograft optionality.

Retail pharmacy network expansion and monetisation: network reached ~780 stores in FY2026 (up 86 stores), with TerryWhite Chemmart banner sales of A$2.9B (+9.2%) and dispensing sales +8.5%. Consumer Brands, CareClinics, and Retail Media remain incremental, higher-margin revenue streams layered onto the core wholesale relationship.

Animal Care growth and category expansion: FY2026 Animal Care revenue +34.6%, EBITDA +11.6%. Paringa Pet Foods (completed July 2026) opens the premium fresh/chilled pet food category, extending Black Hawk/VitaPet's addressable market and supporting the pet humanisation/premiumisation thesis.

CSO expanded regime effective from July 2026 (Section 100 Medicines, higher high-cost medicine cap from A$54 to A$223 per script) now live and expected to support GOR growth and margin through FY2027.

Active bolt-on M&A funded from operating cash flow rather than new equity: eight bolt-on acquisitions completed in FY2026 for a combined A$121M, spanning Retail Pharmacy, Healthcare Distribution, Animal Care, and Medical Technology, with management citing ~A$150M of further bolt-on capacity for FY2027 without new capital raising.

FY2027 EBITDA guidance raised to A$635-655M (~5% growth at the midpoint), explicitly attributed to increased network utilisation/productivity in Symbion & Healthcare Distribution, earnings expansion in Retail Pharmacy Brands, continued MedTech therapy/geographic expansion, and new product/customer growth in Animal Care -- with Retail Pharmacy, MedTech and Animal Care all guided to grow faster than the group average.

business.risk: Recurring pattern of large-customer contract losses to Chemist Warehouse
business.description: Following the 2024 loss of the ~A$1.9B Australian wholesale contract (~10% of group revenue), EBOS's smaller New Zealand wholesale contract with Chemist Warehouse is now scheduled to roll off at the end of calendar 2026. Management sizes the impact at only mid-to-high single-digit A$ millions of EBITDA (~1% of group), so this instance is not thesis-breaking, but it reinforces that Chemist Warehouse's strategy of vertically integrating supply as it scales is a structural, recurring risk to EBOS's largest single wholesale relationship across both markets.

business.risk: Persistent GOR margin compression despite strong revenue growth
business.description: FY2026 group GOR margin fell 40bps to 12.9% on GLP-1/high-value-medicine mix shift; Healthcare EBITDA grew only 3.2% against 8.5% revenue growth, continued negative operating leverage. The 1PWA cap structure on high-value medicines limits GOR margin capture. While management points to DC productivity gains and the expanded CSO regime as offsets, the margin trajectory has yet to visibly turn in the reported numbers.

The April 2026 guidance downgrade (to A$610-620M from A$615-635M) was driven by elevated fuel and hydrocarbon-related consumable costs that EBOS could not fully pass through due to government contract structures. FY2026 landed within the reduced range, and the issue was not repeated in FY2027 guidance commentary, suggesting it was largely transient, but the underlying inability to quickly recover cost inflation remains a structural feature of the model.

Sigma-Chemist Warehouse (35-40% Australian wholesale share) and API-Priceline (Wesfarmers-owned) remain formidable vertically integrated competitors with capital resources to pressure wholesale pricing and independent pharmacy loyalty.

Ongoing PBS price reforms in Australia and PHARMAC pricing pressures in New Zealand reduce drug prices over time, though GLP-1 and specialty medicine volume/value growth continues to more than offset this at the revenue line.

financial.risk: Leverage moderated but still elevated post investment cycle
financial.description: Leverage was 2.1x at FY2026 year-end (within the 1.7-2.3x target range and down from 2.2x at H1 FY2026), aided by FY2026 free cash flow generation. With capex now falling to ~A$100M in FY2027 and the DC program complete, leverage should continue trending toward the lower half of the target range absent large M&A.

EBOS reports in Australian dollars but the parent company is incorporated in New Zealand (NZX listed); NZD dividends are declared then converted to AUD for payment. AUD/NZD exchange rate fluctuations impact reported NZD earnings and dividend values. FY2026 results explicitly cited foreign exchange headwinds alongside fuel costs as a drag on underlying EBITDA growth.

financial.risk: Working capital intensity and cash conversion
financial.description: FY2026 underlying free cash flow was A$241M, down from A$302M in FY2025, primarily because the prior year benefited from a one-off ~A$75M working capital release tied to the Chemist Warehouse Australian contract exit. Net working capital increased only A$7M in FY2026 despite 10% revenue growth (cash conversion days stable at ~20), a reasonable underlying result once the prior-year comparison is normalized.

EBOS completed eight bolt-on acquisitions in FY2026 (~A$121M combined), including Paringa Pet Foods and K-Talyst, on top of the H1 FY2026 deals (NGPF, Precision Surgical, AlphaXRT, MediAdvice, Origin Biologics). Deal volume and integration workload remain high even as the DC capital cycle winds down; management indicates a further ~A$150M of bolt-on capacity for FY2027 without new equity.

regulatory.description: The 1PWA framework structurally caps GOR margins on high-value medicines. The expanded CSO regime effective July 2026 (Section 100 Medicines, higher cost cap) is now live and a partial offset, but the fundamental pricing structure still requires government negotiation for material change, and PHARMAC in New Zealand similarly constrains pricing.
Australia maintains pharmacy ownership rules restricting non-pharmacist ownership. Potential regulatory changes could disrupt the TerryWhite Chemmart and MediAdvice retail model.

The Paringa Pet Foods acquisition underwent ACCC review before being approved in 2026, illustrating that even bolt-on deals now attract competition-regulator scrutiny in Australia's consolidating pet food/animal care market.

macro.description: EBOS revenues are tied to government healthcare spending through PBS and PHARMAC. Aging demographics and rising chronic disease prevalence provide structural demand support that is difficult to curtail.

macro.risk: Consumer discretionary spending in Animal Care
macro.description: Animal Care is exposed to consumer spending on premium pet food and veterinary services. Economic softness could pressure trading down to value brands, though FY2026 growth (+34.6% revenue) shows no sign of this yet.

FY2026 results cited foreign exchange headwinds as a drag alongside fuel costs. Net finance costs remain a function of the Australian cash rate and EBOS's debt funding; with capex and leverage now declining, sensitivity to rates should moderate somewhat into FY2027.

execution.description: The core remaining execution risk has shifted from 'will the DC program finish on time' (now resolved) to 'will the promised productivity and margin benefits actually show up.' Management's own target is a 30% Kemps Creek productivity uplift by end of FY2027 versus ~20% achieved to date; FY2027 EBITDA guidance of A$635-655M assumes this materializes alongside continued Retail Pharmacy, MedTech and Animal Care outperformance.

execution.risk: CEO tenure and consistency of guidance delivery
execution.description: Adam Hall (CEO since July 2025) delivered one guidance downgrade (April 2026, fuel-cost driven) but then landed FY2026 within the revised range and raised FY2027 guidance at the August 2026 result, which is a credibility-rebuilding data point after the prior wobble.

execution.risk: Integration of a high volume of bolt-on acquisitions
execution.description: Eight bolt-on deals completed in FY2026 across four different business lines (Retail Pharmacy, Healthcare Distribution, Animal Care, Medical Technology) creates cumulative integration and management-bandwidth risk even though no single deal is individually large.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Healthcare distribution in Australia and New Zealand continues to benefit from strong structural tailwinds: aging demographics, rising PBS expenditure driven by high-value and specialty medicines, continued double-digit GLP-1 volume growth, and increasing medical technology and aesthetics adoption. Pet care industry growth remains robust, reinforced by EBOS's move into fresh/chilled pet food via Paringa.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low to moderate cyclicality. Pharmaceutical distribution is defensive with stable, government-funded demand through economic cycles. Animal Care branded segment has moderate cyclical exposure but showed no signs of softness in FY2026.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate. Leverage improved to 2.1x at FY2026 year-end (within the 1.7-2.3x target) and is set to decline further as FY2027 capex falls to ~A$100M, reducing incremental rate sensitivity versus the peak-investment period.
key_input_costs: Fuel and transport costs (drove the April 2026 guidance downgrade; FY2026 landed within the revised range and the issue was not repeated in FY2027 guidance)
Hydrocarbon-related consumables (plastic wrapping, polystyrene foam for cold chain packaging)
Labor costs (5,700+ employees, logistics workers facing wage inflation in Australia)
Energy costs (cold chain storage and the now-completed DC network are energy-intensive)
Technology and systems investments (post-commissioning optimisation of the DC network continues into FY2027 even though the capital cycle is complete)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Reports in Australian dollars. Parent company incorporated in NZ and listed on NZX; dividends declared in NZD (final dividend NZ 61.5 cents, maintained). AUD/NZD rate movement impacts NZD-translated earnings and dividend values for NZ investors. FY2026 results cited FX as a headwind alongside fuel costs.

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results released: revenue A$13.5B (+9.9%), underlying EBITDA A$614M (+5.0%, within the downgraded A$610-620M guidance range), underlying NPAT ~A$250M, statutory NPAT ~A$225M. Underlying free cash flow A$241M (down from A$302M in FY2025 due to a prior-year one-off ~A$75M Chemist Warehouse working-capital release). Reported free cash flow ~A$204M. Leverage 2.1x, within target range. Final dividend NZ 61.5 cents per share, maintained. Group GOR margin fell 40bps to 12.9% on GLP-1/high-value-medicine mix. Healthcare EBITDA A$516M (+3.2%); Animal Care revenue A$907M (+34.6%), EBITDA A$138M (+11.6%). Stock rose ~5.5% on the day of results, though it remains well below its 52-week high.

Management confirmed COMPLETION of the four-year, A$360M distribution centre renewal program -- the single largest capital investment cycle in the company's history. Kemps Creek (largest, most complex site) is running approximately 20% more productively than the Greystanes facility it replaced, with a target of 30% productivity uplift by the end of FY2027.

FY2027 underlying EBITDA guidance issued at A$635-655M (~5% growth at the midpoint), an increase versus the pace implied by FY2026, with FY2027 capex guided down to approximately A$100M (from ~A$145M in FY2026), a roughly 30% reduction reflecting completion of the DC renewal program. Guidance assumes no new acquisitions; management cited ~A$150M of additional bolt-on M&A capacity. Divisional outlook: Symbion & Healthcare Distribution to grow slightly below group average; Retail Pharmacy Brands, Medical Technology and Animal Care to grow faster.

Management disclosed that EBOS's smaller New Zealand wholesale contract with Chemist Warehouse is scheduled to roll off at the end of calendar 2026. Impact sized at mid-to-high single-digit A$ millions of EBITDA, approximately 1% of group EBITDA -- materially smaller than the 2024 Australian contract loss (~10% of group revenue) but a reminder of recurring customer-concentration risk with this counterparty.

Completed acquisition of Paringa Pet Foods (premium fresh/chilled pet food), following ACCC merger review clearance. Extends the branded Animal Care portfolio (Black Hawk, VitaPet) into a new, growing category. Financial terms not disclosed; funded within FY2026's broader ~A$121M bolt-on M&A envelope.

Acquired K-Talyst, a distributor of medical devices and aesthetics across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong, accelerating EBOS's entry into the high-growth aesthetics sector and extending Medical Technology's Southeast Asia footprint. One of eight bolt-on acquisitions completed in FY2026 for a combined ~A$121M.

Final FY2026 dividend of NZ 61.5 cents per share confirmed (maintained versus prior year); record date 28 August, payment date 18 September 2026. Separately, former CEO John Cullity sold approximately 236,000 shares (~86% of his direct holding) on-market in September 2026 at approximately NZ$29.67 -- the largest insider sale in the prior three months, though consistent with a retired executive diversifying rather than a signal tied to new information.

FY2026 underlying EBITDA guidance downgraded to A$610-620M (from A$615-635M) due to elevated fuel prices and hydrocarbon-related consumable costs from global supply disruptions. Stock fell modestly (~2.4%) on the news. FY2026 actual result of A$614M landed within this revised range, and the issue was not cited as a recurring factor in FY2027 guidance.

Consolidated control of Origin Biologics (US allograft solutions business) through step acquisition; bank facility refinancing (A$300M due Dec-2026 refinanced to A$400M maturing Dec-2032, extending weighted average debt maturity to 3.3 years); acquired AlphaXRT (radiation oncology) and Precision Surgical (spine implants, NSW).

items.vs_prior: new guidance (raised versus the pace of FY2026 growth)
items.notes: Midpoint A$645M implies ~5% growth on FY2026's A$614M actual. Growth drivers cited: increased network utilisation/productivity in Symbion & Healthcare Distribution, earnings expansion in Retail Pharmacy Brands, continued therapy/geographic expansion in Medical Technology, and new product/customer growth in Animal Care. Guidance assumes no new acquisitions.

items.vs_prior: delivered within the downgraded A$610-620M range
items.notes: Confirms the April 2026 downgrade (from A$615-635M) was not repeated or worsened; all FY2026 guidance metrics were delivered within stated ranges per management.

Down from ~A$145M in FY2026 (final year of the DC renewal program), a ~30% reduction consistent with prior guidance that FY2027 capex would fall roughly 30% following program completion. Direct driver of the expected free cash flow inflection.

items.vs_prior: reaffirmed direction, now against a completed capex cycle
items.notes: FY2026 underlying FCF was A$241M (down from A$302M in FY2025, which included a ~A$75M one-off working-capital benefit from the Chemist Warehouse Australia contract exit); reported FCF ~A$204M. Management continues to guide earnings and cash flows weighted toward H2 in FY2027.

items.target: Payout consistent with 60-80% of underlying NPAT framework
items.notes: FY2026 final dividend NZ 61.5 cents per share, maintained versus prior year, despite underlying EPS softness -- signals Board confidence in the FY2027 cash flow outlook.
Leverage at 2.1x at FY2026 year-end, down from 2.2x at H1 FY2026, within target range. Expected to continue trending lower in FY2027 as capex falls and free cash flow improves, absent large M&A.
Management quantified remaining balance-sheet capacity for further bolt-on acquisitions without new equity issuance, following ~A$121M deployed across eight bolt-on deals in FY2026.

guidance.management_commentary: Management framed FY2026 as the completion of EBOS's largest-ever investment cycle, with the DC renewal program finished on time and within its A$360M budget, and characterized FY2027 as the year the balance sheet and cash flow benefits begin to show through: capex down ~30%, continued mid-single-digit underlying EBITDA growth, and ongoing capacity for disciplined bolt-on M&A (~A$150M) without further equity raising. The tone was notably more confident than the April 2026 downgrade commentary, with the fuel-cost headwind characterized as contained to FY2026 and not carried into FY2027 guidance. Management continues to flag the small New Zealand Chemist Warehouse wholesale contract roll-off (end of calendar 2026) as a manageable, already-guided-for item rather than a surprise.

bull_case: DC investment cycle is now confirmed COMPLETE, not merely on track: the A$360M, four-year program finished on time and within budget in FY2026, FY2027 capex guidance was cut ~30% to ~A$100M, and FY2027 underlying EBITDA guidance was RAISED to A$635-655M -- the coiled-spring free-cash-flow thesis has begun converting into guided numbers rather than remaining a forward promise.

Kemps Creek productivity is already visible in the data (~20% more productive than the facility it replaced, targeting 30% by end of FY2027), giving management-cited operational proof points rather than pure assertion, supporting confidence in the margin-recovery leg of the thesis.

GLP-1 and high-value medicine volumes continue to grow at double-digit rates with no sign of deceleration, and the expanded CSO regime (effective July 2026) is now live and should support GOR economics through FY2027 -- a structural tailwind still largely ahead of the company rather than behind it.

Significant valuation reset: the stock trades roughly 30-45% below its 52-week high and consensus price targets, while trimmed, still imply meaningful upside from the current ~NZ$29-30 level (average target ~NZ$29.60-31.40, some estimates as high as ~NZ$36); a Buy-leaning consensus (7 buy/3 strong buy out of 12 analysts) persists even after the de-rating.

Disciplined, self-funded bolt-on M&A continues to add optionality (Paringa in fresh/chilled pet food, K-Talyst in Southeast Asia aesthetics) without diluting shareholders or raising fresh equity, funded from within a ~A$150M FY2027 capacity envelope while leverage (2.1x) sits comfortably within target range.
Maintained dividend (NZ 61.5 cents final, flat YoY) despite a softer underlying EPS print signals Board confidence that the FY2027 cash flow inflection is real and near-term, not a multi-year story.
bear_case: The market has voted with its feet: despite the DC program completing successfully and FY2027 guidance being raised, the stock has fallen sharply (roughly 30-45% off its 52-week high, analyst targets trimmed from the ~NZ$33-38 range six months ago to ~NZ$29.60-31.40 now), suggesting sophisticated investors remain skeptical that the promised margin/cash-flow inflection will fully materialize, or that GLP-1/high-value-medicine mix economics are structurally lower-margin than the prior wholesale model.

GOR margin compression is not yet turning: FY2026 group GOR margin fell a further 40bps to 12.9%, and Healthcare EBITDA grew only 3.2% against 8.5% revenue growth -- the negative operating leverage that has persisted through the DC build-out has not yet visibly reversed in the reported numbers, leaving the FY2027 recovery still to be proven rather than observed.

A second Chemist Warehouse contract loss (New Zealand wholesale, rolling off end of calendar 2026) — while small in isolation (~1% of group EBITDA) — reinforces a pattern of this customer exiting EBOS relationships as it scales its own vertically integrated supply chain, raising the question of what happens to any remaining Chemist Warehouse-adjacent business over time.

FY2026 underlying free cash flow declined year-on-year (A$241M vs A$302M in FY2025), and while the comparison is distorted by a one-off prior-year working-capital benefit, it means the 'FCF inflection' narrative has not yet shown up in a clean, comparable annual print — FY2027 is still the first real test.

Elevated deal volume (eight bolt-on acquisitions in FY2026 across four different business lines) sustains integration and management-bandwidth risk even as the larger capital program winds down, and FY2027 guidance explicitly excludes any benefit from further M&A, meaning any slippage in bolt-on execution has no guided offset.

Structural margin ceiling under the 1PWA framework and continuing customer-concentration dynamics with large integrated players (Sigma-Chemist Warehouse, Wesfarmers-API) mean that even a successful DC-driven cost reduction may only partially offset ongoing GOR margin pressure from medicine mix shift, capping the pace of EBITDA margin recovery investors are hoping for.
